title: How Daylight Saving Time Affects Health
credits: I’m Caty Weaver. Lauran Neergaard reported on this story for the Associated Press. John Russell adapted it for VOA Learning English. __________________________________________________

sentences.en: Much of the United States “springs forward” on Sunday, March 9th, for daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 美国大部分地区将在3月9日星期日'向前拨快'时钟，进入夏令时。

sentences.en: Worldwide, many other countries also observe daylight saving time, starting and ending on different dates.
sentences.zh: worldwide，许多其他国家也实行夏令时，但开始和结束的日期各不相同。

sentences.en: The time change can leave people tired and perhaps unhappy the next day.
sentences.zh: 时间的改变可能让人第二天感到疲倦，甚至有些不愉快。

sentences.en: But it also might even harm health.
sentences.zh: 但它甚至可能对健康造成损害。

sentences.en: Some studies have found an increase in heart attacks and strokes right after the March time change.
sentences.zh: 一些研究发现，在3月时间调整后不久，心脏病发作和中风的发病率有所上升。

sentences.en: However, there are ways to ease the effects of the time change, including getting more sunshine.
sentences.zh: 不过，有一些方法可以缓解时间变化带来的影响，包括多晒太阳。

sentences.en: The light helps reset your circadian rhythm for healthful sleep.
sentences.zh: 阳光有助于重置你的生物钟，从而获得健康的睡眠。

sentences.en: In the U.S., daylight saving time begins Sunday at 2:00 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 在美国，夏令时从周日凌晨2点开始。

sentences.en: The time change will reverse on November 2 when clocks “fall back” as daylight saving time ends.
sentences.zh: 随着夏令时在11月2日结束，时钟将'向后拨回'，时间调整也随之逆转。

sentences.en: The state of Hawaii and most of the state of Arizona do not make the spring change.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷州和亚利桑那州的大部分地区不做春季的时间调整。

sentences.en: Those areas remain on standard time along with Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
sentences.zh: 这些地区与波多黎各、美属萨摩亚、关岛和美属维尔京群岛一样，仍使用标准时间。

sentences.en: Some people try to prepare for the change to daylight saving time by going to bed a little earlier two or three nights ahead.
sentences.zh: 有些人试图通过提前两三个晚上早睡来为夏令时的到来做准备。

sentences.en: But with a third of American adults already not getting the suggested seven hours of nightly sleep, catching up can be difficult.
sentences.zh: 然而，由于三分之一的美国成年人已经无法获得建议的每晚七小时睡眠，想要补觉可能很困难。

sentences.en: The brain has a kind of clock that is set by exposure to sunlight and darkness.
sentences.zh: 大脑中有一种时钟，它通过接触阳光和黑暗来设定。

sentences.en: This clock, known as the circadian rhythm, is on a roughly 24-hour cycle.
sentences.zh: 这种被称为生物钟的机制大约以24小时为一个周期。

sentences.en: It governs when we become sleepy and when we are more wakeful.
sentences.zh: 它决定了我们何时变得困倦，何时更加清醒。

sentences.en: The rhythms change with age.
sentences.zh: 这些节律会随年龄变化。

sentences.en: This is one reason that early-to-rise young children turn into hard-to-wake teenagers.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么早睡早起的幼儿会逐渐变成难以唤醒的青少年的原因之一。

sentences.en: Morning light resets the rhythm.
sentences.zh: 早晨的光线能够重置生物钟。

sentences.en: By evening, levels of a hormone called melatonin begin to increase, leading to tiredness.
sentences.zh: 到了傍晚，一种名为褪黑素的激素水平开始上升，从而导致困倦。

sentences.en: Too much light in the evening — that extra hour from daylight saving time — delays the melatonin increase.
sentences.zh: 晚上光线过多——夏令时多出来的那个小时——会推迟褪黑素的增加。

sentences.en: As a result, the cycle gets delayed.
sentences.zh: 因此，生物节律会被推迟。

sentences.en: The circadian rhythm affects more than sleep.
sentences.zh: 生物钟影响的不仅仅是睡眠。

sentences.en: It also influences heart rate, blood pressure, hormone releases and other systems.
sentences.zh: 它还会影响心率、血压、激素分泌以及其他系统。

sentences.en: Sleep deprivation, or lack of sleep, is linked to heart disease, weight conditions, problems with thinking and remembering, and more.
sentences.zh: 睡眠不足或缺乏睡眠与心脏病、体重问题、思维和记忆障碍以及更多疾病有关。

sentences.en: Deadly car crash numbers increase the first few days after the spring time change, a study of U.S. traffic deaths says.
sentences.zh: 美国一项关于交通死亡的研究显示，春季时变后的头几天，致命车祸数量会增加。

sentences.en: The risk of crashes is highest in the morning, it found.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，车祸风险在早晨最高。

sentences.en: Researchers suggested sleep deprivation might be responsible.
sentences.zh: 研究人员推测，睡眠不足可能是罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: The time change also has a link to the heart.
sentences.zh: 时变还与心脏有关。

sentences.en: The American Heart Association points to studies that suggest an increase in heart attacks on the Monday after daylight saving time begins, and in strokes for two days afterward.
sentences.zh: 美国心脏协会指出，一些研究表明，夏令时开始后的第一个星期一，心脏病发作会增加，而中风则在之后的两天内增多。

sentences.en: Doctors already know that heart attacks, especially severe ones, are a bit more common on Mondays generally — and in the morning, when blood is more likely to clot.
sentences.zh: 医生早就知道，心脏病发作，尤其是严重的发作，通常在星期一更为常见——而且在早晨，此时血液更容易凝结。

sentences.en: Researchers do not know why the time change would add to that Monday connection.
sentences.zh: 研究人员并不知道，时变为何会加剧这种与星期一的关联。

sentences.en: But it is possible the sudden circadian change influences other issues such as high blood pressure in people already at risk.
sentences.zh: 但有可能，这种突然的生物钟变化会影响其他问题，例如对已有风险的人群而言的高血压。

sentences.en: To prepare for daylight saving time, experts offer some advice.
sentences.zh: 为了迎接夏令时，专家提供了一些建议。

sentences.en: Slowly move bedtimes about 15 or 20 minutes earlier for several nights before the time change.
sentences.zh: 在时变前的几个晚上，把睡觉时间慢慢提前15或20分钟。

sentences.en: Try to rise earlier the next morning, too.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上也尽量更早起床。

sentences.en: Go outside for early morning sunshine the first week of daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 在夏令时的第一周，去迎接清晨的阳光。

sentences.en: This is another way to help reset your body’s clock.
sentences.zh: 这是帮助重置你身体时钟的另一种方式。

sentences.en: Start daily activities, like dinner or exercise, a little earlier.
sentences.zh: 把日常活动，比如晚餐或锻炼，稍微提前一些开始。

sentences.en: This may help tell your body to start getting used to the new conditions, sleep experts suggest.
sentences.zh: 睡眠专家建议，这或许能帮助你身体逐渐适应新的状况。

sentences.en: Daytime sleeping, the drug caffeine and light from phones and other electronic devices can make an earlier bedtime even harder.
sentences.zh: 白天睡觉、药物咖啡因以及手机和其他电子设备发出的光线，会让更早睡的就寝时间变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Americans have discussed ending daylight saving time.
sentences.zh: 美国人已经讨论了废除夏令时。

sentences.en: But so far, no official changes have been made.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，尚未做出任何官方更改。

sentences.en: Health groups such as the American Medical Association and American Academy of Sleep Medicine believe it is time to end time changes.
sentences.zh: 美国医学会和美国睡眠医学协会等健康组织认为，现在到了结束时制变更的时候。

sentences.en: The groups suggest that staying with standard time year-round works better for human biology and sleep needs.
sentences.zh: 这些组织建议，全年采用标准时间更符合人体生物学和睡眠需求。

glossary.def: the mental, behavioral, and physical changes a person experiences over a 24-hour period exposure – n. the condition of being subject to some effect or influence reverse – v. to undo, to turn about in position or direction cycle – n. a series of events that take place regularly and return to the same starting point hormone – n. a product of living cells that circulates in the body and produces an effect on the activity of cells clot – v. to undergo chemical reactions that result in blood becoming a lump or mass (a clot)
